the July 2021 release reported nearly 60 million eligible children and about $15 billion paid."},{"kind":"tool","tool":"official.lookup","call":"Fetched public IRS-derived reference-class summaries from National Academies, CRS, and Tax Foundation.","result":"Fetched National Academies table citing IRS Table 3.3 reports refundable portion of CTC/ACTC number of returns of 20.45 million in 2018 and 37.77 million in 2021, with amounts of $40.72 billion and $115.87 billion in 2021 dollars. Fetched CRS/TPC table reports in 2022 that 89.6% of taxpayers with children received the child credit, including 49.5% under $10,000 income, 63.0% at $10,000-$20,000, and 78.2% at $20,000-$30,000. Fetched Tax Foundation IRS-derived ACTC summary reports 18.921 million ACTC returns for 2016."},{"kind":"text","text":"Base rate/reference class: I anchor on the post-TCJA partial-refundability base around 20.45 million 2018 refundable CTC/ACTC returns, because that is the closest modern non-ARPA regime with a low earnings threshold and similar credit architecture. The 2021 fully refundable 37.77 million return count and 36.049 million advance-payment returns are ceiling references, not the central case, because the conditional threshold change does not remove the earned-income formula or all filing/take-up frictions."},{"kind":"math","text":"Prior/update/interval: persistence prior = 20.45 million claims from 2018 IRS Table 3.3-derived reference, historical sample = 2016 ACTC 18.921, 2018 refundable CTC/ACTC 20.45, 2021 full-refundable 37.77, and 2021 advance-payment 36.049 million. A formal time-series model is not used because the usable regime-consistent sample is sparse and structurally broken by ARPA. Adjustment components: +0.4 million demographic/filing drift from 2018 to TY2027, +1.1 million for families with earnings from $1 to $2,500 who gain small refundable amounts, -0.6 million because some newly eligible units have too little benefit, missing SSNs, no return filing, or no qualifying child under the 2027 rules. Point = 20.45 + 0.4 + 1.1 - 0.6 = 21.35, rounded to 21.4 million. For interval sizing, use stable-regime changes rather than the one-year ARPA regime jump: 2016 to 2018 change = 20.45 - 18.921 = 1.529 million; explicit judgmental policy-mechanism uncertainty add-on = 0.65 million, so sigma = sqrt(1.529^2 + 0.65^2) = 1.66 million. 1.28*sigma = 2.13 million; I widen to 2.8 million because the target is conditional on a new law and IRS first-print take-up can deviate, giving 21.4 +/- 2.8 = 18.6 to 24.2 million."},{"kind":"text","text":"Mechanism check: lowering the threshold from $2,500 to $1 mostly creates small ACTC amounts for workers below the current phase-in threshold; it does not replicate ARPA full refundability for zero-income families. The 2022 low-income recipient rates from CRS/TPC imply substantial remaining headroom among families under $20,000, but only a subset of that headroom is caused by the threshold rather than no filing, no qualifying child, SSN rules, phaseouts, or age limits."},{"kind":"text","text":"Counter-considerations: upside risk is a companion simplification or outreach policy that induces many more low-income families to file, which would land above the interval if claims approach 25 million or more. Downside risk is tight SSN enforcement, weak filing take-up, or a law that technically lowers the threshold but preserves other formula limits, which would land below the interval if claims stay near the 2016-2018 ACTC base under 18.6 million. A full-refundability policy like ARPA would be outside the interval on the upside and should be treated as a different regime."},{"kind":"text","text":"Review disposition: accepted the resolver critique by removing any same-day correction, withdrawal, or accessibility exception from the rule; accepted the interval critique by adding the public source for the 2016 18.921 million value and labeling the 0.65 million component as an explicit judgmental policy-mechanism uncertainty add-on. Also accepted the optional clarification that a formal time-series model is inappropriate for this sparse, structurally broken sample."},{"kind":"forecast","point":21.4,"ciLow":18.6,"ciHigh":24.2}]}
